The annual global temperature anomaly compares each year with the 1951–1980 average. It is a departure from that baseline, not an absolute temperature.

```chart
type: line
title: Global temperature has risen since the late nineteenth century
data: { csv: data/global-temperature.csv }
encoding: { x: year, y: anomaly_c }
axes:
  x: { format: year }
  y: { label: Temperature anomaly, unit: °C }
```

*Source: [NASA GISS GISTEMP v4](https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/), annual land–ocean temperature index, downloaded 9 November 2026. Credit: NASA GISS GISTEMP Team.*

## Read the baseline correctly

Zero means the 1951–1980 average. A value of 1 means one degree Celsius above that baseline. It does not mean an absolute temperature of one degree. This is an annual global index; individual places and months differ. The frozen CSV ends in 2025, so it does not mix an incomplete current year with completed annual means.
